changelog:
[B][COLOR ff00fa9a]Version 1.0.83[/COLOR][/B]
[COLOR fffdb515]The source list now reads the rare things a release name declares[/COLOR]
-A release name is the only thing known about a file before it plays, and the add-on was reading everything in it except the parts that matter most to anyone who cares about them.
-Now read: AV1; the Dolby Vision profile and layer when the name states it (P5, P7, P8, FEL, MEL, hybrid); 10-bit; and 50 or 60 frames per second. AV1 had a badge, a skin rule and a ranker feature already, but nothing was writing the tag for them to find.
-These are the ones drawn in the accent colour, and that is the point of them. Not every device plays profile 5, and plenty cannot handle AV1 at all - the name says so, but it says so in the middle of forty other characters and it gets missed. Now it is the first thing on the row.
-What this cannot do, said plainly: FEL lives in the file's RPU, not in its name. A name that stays quiet cannot be confirmed or contradicted from here. This reads what the name claims, and nothing more.
[COLOR fffdb515]Audio is written as one thing, because it is one thing[/COLOR]
-Atmos over TrueHD in 7.1 used to occupy three separate slots divided by bars, as though unrelated. It now reads ATMOS-TRUE HD (7.1), with DD+ as DOLBY DIGITAL PLUS, DTS-HD MA as DTS-MASTER AUDIO, and the channel count in the form people actually say - 7.1, 5.1, 2.0 - rather than 8CH or 6CH.
-Audio stays in ordinary grey. It belongs on the row as information, not as something demanding attention.
[COLOR fffdb515]Three ways of writing things that were being missed[/COLOR]
-HDR10P, with no plus sign, was being read as plain HDR and the distinction was lost. DDPA - Dolby Digital Plus with Atmos, written without a break - was recognised as neither, leaving the channel count stranded with no codec to belong to.
-And HDR10+ could never be detected by the DMM provider at all: the name clean-up pass replaces every non-alphanumeric character with a full stop, so the plus sign was gone before anything looked at it. DMM was the only one of eighteen scrapers not calling the reader that works on the untouched name.
[COLOR fffdb515]Unusual tags come first on the row[/COLOR]
-The source list only scrolls the row you have highlighted; every other row has its text cut off at the edge. Anything sitting at the end of a long line did not exist until you landed on it, which is exactly where the rarest tags were ending up. They are moved to the front now.
-Nothing is filtered, hidden or reordered by any of this. The list holds what it always held, in the same order.
[COLOR fffdb515]The icon strip no longer depends on how the row is worded[/COLOR]
-Flag images were drawn by matching text against the same string the row displays, so wording and icons were silently tied together and renaming a tag for readability would have switched icons off with no error. The raw tags now live in their own property and the skin matches against that.
